items.text: Tracked parcel #8841-KX is running two days late due to a sorting backlog at the Bellhaven depot; please expect delivery by Thursday. Heroux & Pike's support bot has the same status if you refresh the tracking page.

Heads up that the customer portal will be in read-only mode from 22:00 to 23:30 UTC tonight while we fail over to the secondary database cluster. The status page will update automatically, and the on-call administrator has been paged for the window. If you see a 503 error, please wait five minutes and reload — do not reply to the automated maintenance email, it is sent from a no-reply address. We're treating this as urgent for the payments team only; other modules should stay available.

Your gym membership at Coreline Fitness auto-renews on 14 March; to cancel, visit the front desk or use the member portal before the 10th. The club's chatbot on the website can also walk you through the cancellation steps.

During last night's outage, roughly 40% of API requests to the eastern region returned 502 errors between 01:12 and 02:47 UTC. Our incident report lists the root cause as a failed certificate rotation on the ingress layer, and the fix has been deployed and verified. A follow-up review is scheduled for Friday, and the engineering lead will share the timeline for the promised SLA credits. If your integration still shows stale connection errors, flush your DNS cache and retry — no action is needed on the billing side.

The gym's front-desk system was down for about three hours on Tuesday, so staff wrote check-ins on paper and some class bookings didn't sync. Coreline has since restored the system and says no one will be charged for the missed sessions. If your app still shows a wrong visit count, the support chatbot can file a correction for you, or you can ask at the desk. We're sorry for the confusion and appreciate everyone's patience.

Hi Marta — quick update on the shipment of the replacement treadmill belts for the north branch. The carrier (Northline Freight) says the pallet missed the Tuesday linehaul because of a scanner fault at their hub, so it's now due Friday morning instead of tomorrow. I've marked it urgent in our system, but honestly there's not much we can do beyond waiting.

In the meantime, the two belts we had in stock are with the technician, so the cardio floor should be back to normal by the weekend. If you get questions from members, the front-desk chatbot has the updated ETA and can log complaints.

Do not reply to the carrier's tracking email — it comes from a no-reply address and bounces. Send me anything you need directly.

Thanks,
Priya

Ticket #44127 (server outage, eastern region) has been closed after 36 hours; the postmortem is attached to the status page. The administrator on duty confirmed that all queued jobs have been reprocessed.

We want to apologize for the disruption to Coreline Fitness members this week. A power failure at our data centre took down the check-in system and the class-booking app for most of Tuesday, and some members were turned away at the door even though they had valid memberships.

The outage also affected the automated assistant that answers questions on our website, which gave a few people outdated class times. That's been corrected, and the assistant now pulls from the same schedule staff see at the desk. If you were charged for a session you couldn't attend, please email billing@corelinefitness.example with your member number and we'll reverse it.

We know "urgent" is a strong word, but for anyone training for the spring half-marathon, we've added two extra morning spin classes next week to make up for the lost sessions. The full schedule is on the portal.

Thank you for bearing with us.
Coreline Fitness Member Services
Reminder: the parcel locker code for order #55120 expires in 48 hours; after that the item returns to the depot. This inbox is automated — do not reply.

Status page update — Eastern region API outage (resolved)

Between 01:12 and 02:47 UTC on 9 March, the eastern region API returned 502 errors for approximately 40% of requests. The cause was a failed certificate rotation on the ingress layer. The ingestion and reporting services were degraded for the same window, and some scheduled jobs were delayed by up to three hours.

All services are now healthy. Queued jobs have been reprocessed, and the certificate rotation has been moved to a canary step so a failure can't take the whole region down again. The on-call administrator has posted the timeline and a short postmortem on the engineering wiki; a public summary will follow on Friday.

If your integration still shows stale errors, flush DNS and retry. Customers with questions about SLA credits should contact their account manager rather than replying to this automated notice.
